DC-2025-B260814.aiSummary: The measure would symbolically name the 700-800 block of Euclid Street NW, between Sherman Avenue NW and Georgia Avenue NW in Ward 1, as Dolores Tucker Way. It would honor Dolores Tucker by giving that street block her name. The act would take effect after mayoral approval, council override if needed, a 30-day congressional review, and publication in the District of Columbia Register.

The other is for the Anacostia Boathouse site at 1900 M Street, S.E., extending the lease from June 7, 2030, to June 7, 2047.

DC-2025-CER260236.title: Talib Shakir Recognition Resolution of 2026

actions.text: Retained by the Council
CER26-0236 Introduced by Councilmember R. White at Office of the Secretary

DC-2025-CER260236.aiSummary: This resolution would honor and celebrate the life and service of Talib Shakir, a District resident who helped returning citizens rebuild their lives after incarceration. It recognizes his work in city government, including roles in community relations, safer neighborhoods, and the Office on Returning Citizen Affairs. The Council also expresses condolences to his family and others who loved him.

DC-2025-B260597.aiSummary: The bill would create a new Housing Opportunity Fund for affordable housing in D.C. and split it into accounts for new building, subsidies, preservation, tenant purchases, and public land deals. It would also set rules for how the fund is used, reviewed, and audited, and create a board to help watch over it. The bill would let District retirement funds invest in local real estate, expand the District’s power to acquire land for housing, create a land purchase program and a revolving construction loan fund, and change some purchase rights for certain housing properties.

B26-0847 Introduced by Councilmember Lewis George at Office of the Secretary

DC-2025-B260847.aiSummary: This emergency measure would change the District’s green building rules for some District-owned and District-funded projects. It would exempt certain projects from net-zero-energy rules, update which projects must meet them, and set new rules for some new buildings and major alterations called Level 3 alterations, which are bigger building changes. It also would change deadlines for final rules on net-zero energy and on-site fuel use, which means burning fuel at the building for heat.

DC-2025-B260784.aiSummary: The act became law and makes short-term changes to police complaint rules and some District criminal law terms. It would expand the Police Complaints Board to 9 members and let the Office of Police Complaints’ Executive Director start a complaint based on evidence they find, including missed reports or failure to step in when another officer used excessive force or broke rules. It also changes some District law language so certain provisions apply only to victims under 18.
